text.text_excerpt: We stumbled into this place while cruising Bourbon street. We didn't intend to stop, but was we were walking by, the sounds of a live funk bad playing a jamming cover got our attention. We were really there for the band, and not much else. The beers were cheap enough, I guess. There were girls running around trying to get people to buy jello shots...not typically my scene. But the band was awesome! We went there twice and found out they are pretty regular performers there. They definitely know how to get the crowd moving.

On Bourbon Street we heard a lot of live bands playing rock and country, but we heard some good funk music coming out of here, so naturally we brought our funky asses here. The live band playing that night were playing a lot of good 70's and 80's funk, from Rick James to Earth Wind and Fire. They were pretty fun, and had the crowd going! Drinks were pretty cheap, and there was a shot girl selling shots where she pretty much puts the tube in her mouth and you put the open side of the tube on your mouth and she pours the shot in to your mouth. I hope I explained it right, but just know it's a very flirtatious way of giving a shot haha. There are two floors, the top one with a balcony overlo...

In my most recent visit to New Orleans I've made a lot of memories at Funky 544! On our first night on Bourbon Street I had my fishbowl as a poison of choice. When we came in here DJ was blasting current and throwback hip hop music, wasn't too crowded but it had a good crowd. The MC had the microphone and I was having too much fun that I took the mic from him and started singing and dancing to Chris Brown! We did have a great time even though we were here for a short time because we were bar hopping. Definitely give this place a try if you want to hear the DJ playing, you'll have a great time here.
